impact: The UI uses well-drawn inline lucide-style SVG icons for the dropzone, file row, close chevron, and split grip — then falls back to bare unicode glyphs for HUD buttons: `↺` (replace), `⎘` (copy), `↓` (download), `✕` (dialog close), `?` (about). These render inconsistently across OSes and font stacks (`⎘` especially — often missing or rendered from a different family). Swap them for matching inline SVG icons for a single, consistent icon system.
resolution: Committed in 37acb65. Swapped four unicode glyphs for matching lucide-style stroke=1.75 SVGs (currentColor, aria-hidden): .hud-replace → refresh-cw 12px, .hud-download → download 14px, #copy-btn.hud-copy → copy 14px, .dialog-close → x 14px. Added inline-flex + gap on those four button classes so icon and text align cleanly. .about-btn's `?` left alone — real ASCII rendering everywhere and the button is a 22px circle where a nested circular SVG would read cramped.
title: Inconsistent iconography: unicode glyphs mixed with inline SVG icons
